## 243. pypde\docs\reference\de\app\_autosummary\keysight.ads.de.app.DesignWindowChange.md {#pypde--docs--reference--de--app--_autosummary--keysight.ads.de.app.designwindowchange}

# DesignWindowChange[](#designwindowchange "Link to this heading")

*class* DesignWindowChange[](#keysight.ads.de.app.DesignWindowChange "Link to this definition")
:   Bases: `Enum`

    Specifies the type of change that triggered a DesignWindowCallback.

    Attributes

    |  |  |
    | --- | --- |
    | [`OPENED`](#keysight.ads.de.app.DesignWindowChange.OPENED "keysight.ads.de.app.DesignWindowChange.OPENED") | A design was opened in a new window. |
    | [`CLOSED`](#keysight.ads.de.app.DesignWindowChange.CLOSED "keysight.ads.de.app.DesignWindowChange.CLOSED") | A design window closed. |
    | [`SAVED_AS`](#keysight.ads.de.app.DesignWindowChange.SAVED_AS "keysight.ads.de.app.DesignWindowChange.SAVED_AS") | The design in the window was just saved to a new name. |
    | [`PUSHED`](#keysight.ads.de.app.DesignWindowChange.PUSHED "keysight.ads.de.app.DesignWindowChange.PUSHED") | The design in the window has just been pushed. |
    | [`POPPED`](#keysight.ads.de.app.DesignWindowChange.POPPED "keysight.ads.de.app.DesignWindowChange.POPPED") | The design in the window has just been popped. |

    OPENED *= <DesignWindowChange.OPENED: 0>*[](#keysight.ads.de.app.DesignWindowChange.OPENED "Link to this definition")
    :   A design was opened in a new window.

    CLOSED *= <DesignWindowChange.CLOSED: 1>*[](#keysight.ads.de.app.DesignWindowChange.CLOSED "Link to this definition")
    :   A design window closed.

    SAVED\_AS *= <DesignWindowChange.SAVED\_AS: 2>*[](#keysight.ads.de.app.DesignWindowChange.SAVED_AS "Link to this definition")
    :   The design in the window was just saved to a new name.

        The design with the old name will remain open if modified.

    PUSHED *= <DesignWindowChange.PUSHED: 3>*[](#keysight.ads.de.app.DesignWindowChange.PUSHED "Link to this definition")
    :   The design in the window has just been pushed.

    POPPED *= <DesignWindowChange.POPPED: 4>*[](#keysight.ads.de.app.DesignWindowChange.POPPED "Link to this definition")
    :   The design in the window has just been popped.


---

## 256. pypde\docs\reference\de\app\_autosummary\keysight.ads.de.app.create_layout_palette.md {#pypde--docs--reference--de--app--_autosummary--keysight.ads.de.app.create_layout_palette}

# create\_layout\_palette[](#create-layout-palette "Link to this heading")

create\_layout\_palette(*lib\_name: str*, *group\_name: str*, *items: Sequence[Sequence[str]]*) → None[](#keysight.ads.de.app.create_layout_palette "Link to this definition")
:   Create a palette for the layout window.

    Parameters:
    :   * **lib\_name** (*str*) – The name of the library for this palette.
        * **group\_name** (*str*) – Name of the palette group that will appear in the list of palettes.
        * **items** (*Sequence*) – Each item is a list of the form
          [name, label, bitmap]
          name can be of the form “lib:cell:view” or “lib:cell” or “cell”

    Example

    ```
    bitmap_path: str # has path to the bitmaps

    items = [
    ["demo_mmWave_TECHINCLUDE", "Technology include component", f"{bitmap_path}/demo_mmWave_TECHINCLUDE_BITMAP"],
    ["demo_mmWave_Res", "Resistor", f"{bitmap_path}/demo_mmWave_Res_BITMAP"],
    ["demo_mmWave_Cap", "Capacitor", f"{bitmap_path}/demo_mmWave_Cap_BITMAP"]
    ["demo_mmWave_Ind", "Inductor", f"{bitmap_path}/demo_mmWave_Ind_BITMAP"],
    ["demo_mmWave_FET", "FET", f"{bitmap_path}/demo_mmWave_FET_BITMAP"],
    ["demo_mmWave_Tline", "Tline", f"{bitmap_path}/demo_mmWave_Tline_BITMAP"]
    ]
    app.create_schematic_palette("DemoKit_mmWave", "MM Wave PDK", items)
    ```


---

              Return a [`ParamItem`](keysight.ads.de.db.ParamItem.md#keysight.ads.de.db.ParamItem "keysight.ads.de.db.ParamItem") as the default value.

              [`PARAMETER_MODIFIED`](keysight.ads.de._pde.ModelCbType.md#keysight.ads.de._pde.ModelCbType.PARAMETER_MODIFIED "keysight.ads.de._pde.ModelCbType.PARAMETER_MODIFIED"):

              The callback should modify any dependent parameters as needed.
              Return True if the callback modifies any parameters.

              [`ITEM_NETLIST`](keysight.ads.de._pde.ModelCbType.md#keysight.ads.de._pde.ModelCbType.ITEM_NETLIST "keysight.ads.de._pde.ModelCbType.ITEM_NETLIST"):
              Called when generating a netlist.
              Return the netlist string for this item.

              [`ITEM_MODIFIED`](keysight.ads.de._pde.ModelCbType.md#keysight.ads.de._pde.ModelCbType.ITEM_MODIFIED "keysight.ads.de._pde.ModelCbType.ITEM_MODIFIED"):

              This is essentially an observer - no need to do anything.
              Return None
            * **callback** – The user-supplied function to call

    *static* parameter\_default\_value\_callback(*callback: Callable[[[ModelParam](keysight.ads.de.db.ModelParam.md#keysight.ads.de.db.ModelParam "keysight.ads.de.db.ModelParam"), [ModelDefBase](keysight.ads.de.db.ModelDefBase.md#keysight.ads.de.db.ModelDefBase "keysight.ads.de.db.ModelDefBase"), [Design](../../db_uu/_autosummary/keysight.ads.de.db_uu.Design.md#keysight.ads.de.db_uu.Design "keysight.ads.de.db_uu.Design")], [ParamItem](keysight.ads.de.db.ParamItem.md#keysight.ads.de.db.ParamItem "keysight.ads.de.db.ParamItem")]*) → [ModelCb](#keysight.ads.de.db.ModelCb "keysight.ads.de.db.ModelCb")[](#keysight.ads.de.db.ModelCb.parameter_default_value_callback "Link to this definition")
    :   Create a default value callback for a model parameter.

        Parameters:
        :   **callback** – The user-supplied function with the signature:

        ```
        def callback(
            param: de.db.ModelParam, model_def: de.db.ModelDefBase, design: de.db.Design
        ) -> de.db.ParamItem:
            ...
        ```

        The return value of the callback is the default value for the parameter.

        You can use a lambda if you want a different signature.

        Example

        ```
        def my_default_value_callback(design: de.db.Design) -> de.db.ParamItem:
            if design.units.length_unit == de.db.LengthUnit.MIL:
                return de.db.std_string_param("10 mil")
            else:
                return de.db.std_string_param("0.254 mm")

        # The callback only needs the design, so we use a lambda.
        default_value_cb = de.db.ModelCb.parameter_default_value_callback(
            lambda param, model_def, design: my_default_value_callback(design)
        )
        ```

    *static* parameter\_modified\_callback(*callback: Callable[[[ItemInfo](../../_autosummary/keysight.ads.de.ItemInfo.md#keysight.ads.de.ItemInfo "keysight.ads.de.ItemInfo")], bool]*) → [ModelCb](#keysight.ads.de.db.ModelCb "keysight.ads.de.db.ModelCb")[](#keysight.ads.de.db.ModelCb.parameter_modified_callback "Link to this definition")
    :   Create a parameter modified callback.

        Parameters:
        :   **callback** – The user-supplied function with the signature:

        ```
        def callback(item_info: de.ItemInfo) -> bool:
            ...
        ```

        The return value of the callback should be True if the callback modified any parameters.

        You can use a lambda if you want a different signature.

        Example

        ```
        def my_parameter_modified_callback(item_info: de.ItemInfo) -> bool:
            width = item_info.parameters["Width"].value
            length = item_info.parameters["Length"].value
            area = float(width) * float(length)
            item_info.parameters["Area"].value = str(area)
            return True

        modified_cb = de.db.ModelCb.parameter_modified_callback(
            my_parameter_modified_callback
        )
        ```

    *static* item\_netlist\_callback(*callback: Callable[[[StandardInstance](keysight.ads.de.db.StandardInstance.md#keysight.ads.de.db.StandardInstance "keysight.ads.de.db._callbacks.StandardInstance")], str]*) → [ModelCb](#keysight.ads.de.db.ModelCb "keysight.ads.de.db._callbacks.ModelCb")[](#keysight.ads.de.db.ModelCb.item_netlist_callback "Link to this definition")
    :   Create a netlist callback.

        Parameters:
        :   **callback** – The user-supplied function with the signature:

        ```
        def callback(netlist_inst: de.db.StandardInstance) -> str:
            ...
        ```

        The return value of the callback should be the netlist string for this instance.

        You can use a lambda if you want a different signature.

        Example

        ```
        def my_netlist_callback(netlist_inst: de.db.StandardInstance) -> str:
            from keysight.ads.de.experimental.netlist_helper import NetlistStringBuilder

            builder = NetlistStringBuilder(netlist_inst)
            # Modify this code as needed.
            return builder.clear_and_get_default_netlist_str()

        netlist_cb = de.db.ModelCb.item_netlist_callback(
            my_netlist_callback
        )
        ```

    *static* item\_modified\_callback(*callback: Callable[[[Instance](../../db_uu/_autosummary/keysight.ads.de.db_uu.Instance.md#keysight.ads.de.db_uu.Instance "keysight.ads.de.db_uu.Instance")], None]*) → [ModelCb](#keysight.ads.de.db.ModelCb "keysight.ads.de.db.ModelCb")[](#keysight.ads.de.db.ModelCb.item_modified_callback "Link to this definition")
    :   Create an item modified callback.

        Parameters:
        :   **callback** – The user-supplied function with the signature:

        ```
        def callback(inst: de.db_uu.Instance) -> None:
            ...
        ```

        The callback should be efficient and avoid modifying anything in the design.

        You can use a lambda if you want a different signature.

        Example

        ```
        def my_modified_callback(inst: de.db_uu.Instance) -> None:
            print(f"Instance {inst.name} was modified.")

        modified_cb = de.db.ModelCb.item_modified_callback(
            my_modified_callback
        )
        ```

    *property* enabled*: bool*[](#keysight.ads.de.db.ModelCb.enabled "Link to this definition")
    :   True if this callback is enabled (almost always True).

    *property* type*: [ModelCbType](keysight.ads.de._pde.ModelCbType.md#keysight.ads.de._pde.ModelCbType "keysight.ads.de._pde.ModelCbType")*[](#keysight.ads.de.db.ModelCb.type "Link to this definition")
    :   The type of this callback.

*class* ModelCbBase[](#keysight.ads.de.db.ModelCbBase "Link to this definition")
:   Bases: `object`

    Base class for callbacks used by model definitions and model parameters.

    These callbacks allow customization of model definitions and model
    parameters using either Python or AEL.

    See [`ModelParam`](keysight.ads.de.db.ModelParam.md#keysight.ads.de.db.ModelParam "keysight.ads.de.db.ModelParam") and [`ModelDef`](keysight.ads.de.db.ModelDef.md#keysight.ads.de.db.ModelDef "keysight.ads.de.db.ModelDef").

    This defines the parameters, callbacks and other properties required to
    interpret and edit component instances.

    This is sometimes referred to as an item definition or component definition,
    but [`Term`](../../db_uu/_autosummary/keysight.ads.de.db_uu.Term.md#keysight.ads.de.db_uu.Term "keysight.ads.de.db_uu.Term") also has a shared ModelDef.

## 277. pypde\docs\reference\de\db\_autosummary\keysight.ads.de.db.ModelParam.md {#pypde--docs--reference--de--db--_autosummary--keysight.ads.de.db.modelparam}

# ModelParam[](#modelparam "Link to this heading")

*class* ModelParam[](#keysight.ads.de.db.ModelParam "Link to this definition")
:   Bases: `object`

    ModelParam is a parameter definition that is a part of a model definition (see [`ModelDef`](keysight.ads.de.db.ModelDef.md#keysight.ads.de.db.ModelDef "keysight.ads.de.db.ModelDef")).

    Parameter values are stored in [`ParamItem`](keysight.ads.de.db.ParamItem.md#keysight.ads.de.db.ParamItem "keysight.ads.de.db.ParamItem") objects.
    Parameter values have associated forms that determine how the parameter
    is stored, netlisted and displayed (see [`Form`](keysight.ads.de.db.Form.md#keysight.ads.de.db.Form "keysight.ads.de.db.Form")).
    The allowed forms for a given parameter are listed in its formset (see [`Formset`](keysight.ads.de.db.Formset.md#keysight.ads.de.db.Formset "keysight.ads.de.db.Formset"))

    Methods

    |  |  |
    | --- | --- |
    | [`__init__`](#keysight.ads.de.db.ModelParam.__init__ "keysight.ads.de.db.ModelParam.__init__")(name, label[, formset, unit\_type, ...]) | Initialize a ModelParam. |
    | [`get_default_value_copy`](#keysight.ads.de.db.ModelParam.get_default_value_copy "keysight.ads.de.db.ModelParam.get_default_value_copy")(design, model\_definition) | Get a copy of the default value, invoking the callback if one exists. |
    | [`get_default_value_copy_with_units`](#keysight.ads.de.db.ModelParam.get_default_value_copy_with_units "keysight.ads.de.db.ModelParam.get_default_value_copy_with_units")(design, model) | Get a copy of the default value with units, invoking the callback if one exists. |

    | [`formset`](#keysight.ads.de.db.ModelParam.formset "keysight.ads.de.db.ModelParam.formset") | The set of forms usable by parameters using this definition. |
    | [`is_constant`](#keysight.ads.de.db.ModelParam.is_constant "keysight.ads.de.db.ModelParam.is_constant") | True if this parameter is a constant. |
    | [`is_design_name`](#keysight.ads.de.db.ModelParam.is_design_name "keysight.ads.de.db.ModelParam.is_design_name") | True if this parameter represents the name of a design. |
    | [`is_discrete_value`](#keysight.ads.de.db.ModelParam.is_discrete_value "keysight.ads.de.db.ModelParam.is_discrete_value") | True if this parameter is a discrete value. |

    | [`is_doe`](#keysight.ads.de.db.ModelParam.is_doe "keysight.ads.de.db.ModelParam.is_doe") | True if this parameter is used in Design of Experiments (DOE) sweeps. |

    | [`is_netlist_rhs_only`](#keysight.ads.de.db.ModelParam.is_netlist_rhs_only "keysight.ads.de.db.ModelParam.is_netlist_rhs_only") | True if only the right-hand side of this parameter is netlisted. |
    | [`is_netlistable`](#keysight.ads.de.db.ModelParam.is_netlistable "keysight.ads.de.db.ModelParam.is_netlistable") | True if this parameter is netlistable. |

    | [`is_on_screen_editable`](#keysight.ads.de.db.ModelParam.is_on_screen_editable "keysight.ads.de.db.ModelParam.is_on_screen_editable") | True if this parameter is editable via on-screen editing. |

    | [`unit_type`](#keysight.ads.de.db.ModelParam.unit_type "keysight.ads.de.db.ModelParam.unit_type") | The type of units that apply to parameter values that use this definition. |

    \_\_init\_\_(*name: str*, *label: str*, *formset: [Formset](keysight.ads.de.db.Formset.md#keysight.ads.de.db.Formset "keysight.ads.de.db.Formset") | None = None*, *unit\_type: [ModelUnitType](keysight.ads.de._pde.ModelUnitType.md#keysight.ads.de._pde.ModelUnitType "keysight.ads.de._pde.ModelUnitType") | str | None = None*, *param\_type: [ModelParamType](keysight.ads.de._pde.ModelParamType.md#keysight.ads.de._pde.ModelParamType "keysight.ads.de._pde.ModelParamType") | str | None = None*) → None[](#keysight.ads.de.db.ModelParam.__init__ "Link to this definition")
    :   Initialize a ModelParam.

        Parameters:
        :   * **name** (*str*) – Name of the parameter
            * **label** (*str*) – Descriptive label for the parameter
            * **formset** (*Optional[Formset]*) – A Formset is a list of one or more [`Form`](keysight.ads.de.db.Form.md#keysight.ads.de.db.Form "keysight.ads.de.db.Form") that describe how the parameter
              is stored, how it is netlisted and how it is displayed.
              If not specified, the global StdFormSet will be used.
            * **unit\_type** (*Optional[ModelUnitType]*) – The units of the parameter, defaults to NO\_UNIT (plain numbers)
            * **param\_type** (*Optional[ModelParamType]*) – The datatype of the parameter value, defaults to REAL

    *property* name*: str*[](#keysight.ads.de.db.ModelParam.name "Link to this definition")
    :   The parameter name.

        Changing the name of a definition is dangerous once the parameter is in use.

    *property* label*: str*[](#keysight.ads.de.db.ModelParam.label "Link to this definition")
    :   A descriptive label for the parameter.

    *property* formset*: [Formset](keysight.ads.de.db.Formset.md#keysight.ads.de.db.Formset "keysight.ads.de.db.Formset")*[](#keysight.ads.de.db.ModelParam.formset "Link to this definition")
    :   The set of forms usable by parameters using this definition.

        A Formset is a list of one or more [`Form`](keysight.ads.de.db.Form.md#keysight.ads.de.db.Form "keysight.ads.de.db.Form") that describe how the parameter
        is stored, how it is netlisted and how it is displayed.
        Changing the value of the formset is dangerous if any form is removed
        that was already is in use.

    *property* unit\_type*: [ModelUnitType](keysight.ads.de._pde.ModelUnitType.md#keysight.ads.de._pde.ModelUnitType "keysight.ads.de._pde.ModelUnitType")*[](#keysight.ads.de.db.ModelParam.unit_type "Link to this definition")
    :   The type of units that apply to parameter values that use this definition.

    *property* param\_type*: [ModelParamType](keysight.ads.de._pde.ModelParamType.md#keysight.ads.de._pde.ModelParamType "keysight.ads.de._pde.ModelParamType")*[](#keysight.ads.de.db.ModelParam.param_type "Link to this definition")
    :   The datatype of parameter values that use this definition.

    *property* callbacks*: [ListRefAbc](../../_autosummary/keysight.ads.de._list_like.ListRefAbc.md#keysight.ads.de._list_like.ListRefAbc "keysight.ads.de._list_like.ListRefAbc")[[ModelCbBase](keysight.ads.de.db.ModelCbBase.md#keysight.ads.de.db.ModelCbBase "keysight.ads.de.db._callbacks.ModelCbBase")]*[](#keysight.ads.de.db.ModelParam.callbacks "Link to this definition")
    :   The collection of callbacks in this parameter definition.

    *property* default\_value*: [ParamItem](keysight.ads.de.db.ParamItem.md#keysight.ads.de.db.ParamItem "keysight.ads.de.db.ParamItem") | None*[](#keysight.ads.de.db.ModelParam.default_value "Link to this definition")
    :   The default value for the parameter.

        If the default\_value property is not set, the default value **must** be
        provided by a default value callback (a [`ModelCbBase`](keysight.ads.de.db.ModelCbBase.md#keysight.ads.de.db.ModelCbBase "keysight.ads.de.db.ModelCbBase")
        instance whose [`type`](keysight.ads.de.db.ModelCbBase.md#keysight.ads.de.db.ModelCbBase.type "keysight.ads.de.db.ModelCbBase.type") is
        [`PARAMETER_DEFAULT_VALUE`](keysight.ads.de._pde.ModelCbType.md#keysight.ads.de._pde.ModelCbType.PARAMETER_DEFAULT_VALUE "keysight.ads.de._pde.ModelCbType.PARAMETER_DEFAULT_VALUE")).

        When creating a ModelParam for a ModelDef in Python, the callback will
        be a [`ModelCb`](keysight.ads.de.db.ModelCb.md#keysight.ads.de.db.ModelCb "keysight.ads.de.db.ModelCb")
        (a [`ModelCbBase`](keysight.ads.de.db.ModelCbBase.md#keysight.ads.de.db.ModelCbBase "keysight.ads.de.db.ModelCbBase") implemented in Python).
        When inspecting existing models, this will either be a
        [`ModelCbAEL`](keysight.ads.de.db.ModelCbAEL.md#keysight.ads.de.db.ModelCbAEL "keysight.ads.de.db.ModelCbAEL") for AEL models or a
        [`ModelCb`](keysight.ads.de.db.ModelCb.md#keysight.ads.de.db.ModelCb "keysight.ads.de.db.ModelCb") for Python models.

        If the default\_value property and a
        [`PARAMETER_DEFAULT_VALUE`](keysight.ads.de._pde.ModelCbType.md#keysight.ads.de._pde.ModelCbType.PARAMETER_DEFAULT_VALUE "keysight.ads.de._pde.ModelCbType.PARAMETER_DEFAULT_VALUE")
        default value callback are both set,
        the value returned by the callback will take precedence.

        If you set the default\_value property, the
        [`ParamItem`](keysight.ads.de.db.ParamItem.md#keysight.ads.de.db.ParamItem "keysight.ads.de.db.ParamItem") you pass in as the default
        value may be modified to match the
        parameter definition.

## 279. pypde\docs\reference\de\db\_autosummary\keysight.ads.de.db.ExpressionContext.md {#pypde--docs--reference--de--db--_autosummary--keysight.ads.de.db.expressioncontext}

# ExpressionContext[](#expressioncontext "Link to this heading")

*class* ExpressionContext[](#keysight.ads.de.db.ExpressionContext "Link to this definition")
:   Bases: `object`

    Used for expression evaluation.

    Methods

    |  |  |
    | --- | --- |
    | [`__init__`](#keysight.ads.de.db.ExpressionContext.__init__ "keysight.ads.de.db.ExpressionContext.__init__")() | Initialize an ExpressionContext. |
    | [`clear_design_caches`](#keysight.ads.de.db.ExpressionContext.clear_design_caches "keysight.ads.de.db.ExpressionContext.clear_design_caches")() | Clear all the caches for this design. |
    | [`evaluate_expression`](#keysight.ads.de.db.ExpressionContext.evaluate_expression "keysight.ads.de.db.ExpressionContext.evaluate_expression")(expr, \*[, clear\_caches]) | Evaluate the expression in this expression context and return the result. |
    | [`pop`](#keysight.ads.de.db.ExpressionContext.pop "keysight.ads.de.db.ExpressionContext.pop")() | Pop the top instance off the hierarchy stack. |
    | [`push_instance_for_reading`](#keysight.ads.de.db.ExpressionContext.push_instance_for_reading "keysight.ads.de.db.ExpressionContext.push_instance_for_reading")(inst) | Push the given instance onto the hierarchy stack for reading. |
    | [`setup_hierarchy_for_design`](#keysight.ads.de.db.ExpressionContext.setup_hierarchy_for_design "keysight.ads.de.db.ExpressionContext.setup_hierarchy_for_design")(design) | Set up the hierarchy for the given design. |
    | [`setup_hierarchy_for_layout_only`](#keysight.ads.de.db.ExpressionContext.setup_hierarchy_for_layout_only "keysight.ads.de.db.ExpressionContext.setup_hierarchy_for_layout_only")(design) | Set up the hierarchy for layout only for the given design. |
    | [`update_pcell_params`](#keysight.ads.de.db.ExpressionContext.update_pcell_params "keysight.ads.de.db.ExpressionContext.update_pcell_params")(inst) | Update the PCell parameters of the given instance. |

    Attributes

    |  |  |
    | --- | --- |
    | [`hierarchy_context`](#keysight.ads.de.db.ExpressionContext.hierarchy_context "keysight.ads.de.db.ExpressionContext.hierarchy_context") | The hierarchy context used by this expression context. |
    | [`is_valid`](#keysight.ads.de.db.ExpressionContext.is_valid "keysight.ads.de.db.ExpressionContext.is_valid") | True if the hierarchy has been set up. |

    \_\_init\_\_()[](#keysight.ads.de.db.ExpressionContext.__init__ "Link to this definition")

    \_\_init\_\_(*design: DesignDbu | DesignUu*)
    :   Initialize an ExpressionContext.

        Parameters:
        :   **design** (*Optional[Design]*) – If provided, sets up the hierarchy for the given design.
            If not provided, the hierarchy must be set up prior to using
            the ExpressionContext.

        Example

        ```
        with de.db.ExpressionContext(design) as expr_context:
            expr_context.update_pcell_params(inst)

        with de.db.ExpressionContext() as expr_context:
            expr_context.setup_hierarchy_for_design(design)
            expr_context.evaluate_expression("Width * Length")
        ```

    *property* hierarchy\_context*: [DesignHierarchy](../../_autosummary/keysight.ads.de.DesignHierarchy.md#keysight.ads.de.DesignHierarchy "keysight.ads.de._core.design_hierarchy.DesignHierarchy")*[](#keysight.ads.de.db.ExpressionContext.hierarchy_context "Link to this definition")
    :   The hierarchy context used by this expression context.

        This will return an invalid DesignHierarchy if the hierarchy
        has not been set up.

    :   True if the hierarchy has been set up.

    :   Set up the hierarchy for the given design.

    setup\_hierarchy\_for\_layout\_only(*design: DesignDbu | DesignUu*) → None[](#keysight.ads.de.db.ExpressionContext.setup_hierarchy_for_layout_only "Link to this definition")
    :   Set up the hierarchy for layout only for the given design.

    evaluate\_expression(*expr: str*, *\**, *clear\_caches: bool = False*) → str[](#keysight.ads.de.db.ExpressionContext.evaluate_expression "Link to this definition")
    :   Evaluate the expression in this expression context and return the result.

        If clear\_caches is True, clear all the caches for this design before evaluating.

        Will raise an exception if the hierarchy has not been set up.

    update\_pcell\_params(*inst: InstanceDbu | InstanceUu*) → None[](#keysight.ads.de.db.ExpressionContext.update_pcell_params "Link to this definition")
    :   Update the PCell parameters of the given instance.

    clear\_design\_caches() → None[](#keysight.ads.de.db.ExpressionContext.clear_design_caches "Link to this definition")
    :   Clear all the caches for this design.

        Will raise an exception if the hierarchy has not been set up.

    push\_instance\_for\_reading(*inst: InstanceDbu | InstanceUu*) → None[](#keysight.ads.de.db.ExpressionContext.push_instance_for_reading "Link to this definition")
    :   Push the given instance onto the hierarchy stack for reading.

        This is useful to evaluate expressions in the context of a specific
        instance’s sub-design.

        Will raise an exception if the hierarchy has not been set up.

    pop() → None[](#keysight.ads.de.db.ExpressionContext.pop "Link to this definition")
    :   Pop the top instance off the hierarchy stack.

        Used to return to the previous level in the hierarchy after a push.

        Will raise an exception if the hierarchy has not been set up
        or if you are already at the root of the hierarchy.

        ```

## 284. pypde\docs\reference\de\db\_autosummary\keysight.ads.de.db.ParamItem.md {#pypde--docs--reference--de--db--_autosummary--keysight.ads.de.db.paramitem}

# ParamItem[](#paramitem "Link to this heading")

*class* ParamItem[](#keysight.ads.de.db.ParamItem "Link to this definition")
:   Bases: `object`

    Base class for parameter values (instance-specific value data without a definition).

    A ParamItem represents the stored value of a parameter for a
    particular owner. The concrete value lives on subclasses:

    * [`ParamItemString`](keysight.ads.de.db.ParamItemString.md#keysight.ads.de.db.ParamItemString "keysight.ads.de.db.ParamItemString") stores a string value
    * [`ParamItemConst`](keysight.ads.de.db.ParamItemConst.md#keysight.ads.de.db.ParamItemConst "keysight.ads.de.db.ParamItemConst") has no stored value; its value is determined by its form
    * [`ParamItemCompound`](keysight.ads.de.db.ParamItemCompound.md#keysight.ads.de.db.ParamItemCompound "keysight.ads.de.db.ParamItemCompound") stores a structured value as a collection of sub-items
    * [`ParamItemRepeated`](keysight.ads.de.db.ParamItemRepeated.md#keysight.ads.de.db.ParamItemRepeated "keysight.ads.de.db.ParamItemRepeated") stores a list of one or more repeats (ParamItems)

    ParamItem also stores the selected form (`form_name`), which describes
    how the value is represented. For constant/enumerated parameters, the form
    essentially *is* the value.

    Owners are most commonly an [`Instance`](../../db_uu/_autosummary/keysight.ads.de.db_uu.Instance.md#keysight.ads.de.db_uu.Instance "keysight.ads.de.db_uu.Instance") or [`Term`](../../db_uu/_autosummary/keysight.ads.de.db_uu.Term.md#keysight.ads.de.db_uu.Term "keysight.ads.de.db_uu.Term")
    (DBU equivalents exist in `db_dbu`).

    Valid parameter definitions ([`ModelParam`](keysight.ads.de.db.ModelParam.md#keysight.ads.de.db.ModelParam "keysight.ads.de.db.ModelParam")) are declared
    on a model definition ([`ModelDef`](keysight.ads.de.db.ModelDef.md#keysight.ads.de.db.ModelDef "keysight.ads.de.db.ModelDef")). A ParamItem may
    exist in Python without being paired to its definition, but is always
    implicitly linked with its definition by name. When used by itself,
    it cannot validate whether its form/value choices are compatible with the
    definition, but its `name` and `form_name` are still expected
    to be compatible with the associated definition.

    ParamItem objects are primarily used in two situations:
    - As default values when authoring a parameter definition
    ([`ModelParam`](keysight.ads.de.db.ModelParam.md#keysight.ads.de.db.ModelParam "keysight.ads.de.db.ModelParam"))
    - As the [`ParamBase.item`](keysight.ads.de.db.ParamBase.md#keysight.ads.de.db.ParamBase.item "keysight.ads.de.db.ParamBase.item") half of a definition/value pair
    for editing parameters on an Instance or Term.

    Prefer to use [`ParamBase`](keysight.ads.de.db.ParamBase.md#keysight.ads.de.db.ParamBase "keysight.ads.de.db.ParamBase") (and subclasses) when editing or
    validating parameters, because it provides access to both the item
    and its definition.

    Methods

    |  |  |
    | --- | --- |
    | [`clone`](#keysight.ads.de.db.ParamItem.clone "keysight.ads.de.db.ParamItem.clone")() | Create a copy of this ParamItem. |
    | [`is_compound`](#keysight.ads.de.db.ParamItem.is_compound "keysight.ads.de.db.ParamItem.is_compound")(p) | Return True if the ParamItem is a [`ParamItemCompound`](keysight.ads.de.db.ParamItemCompound.md#keysight.ads.de.db.ParamItemCompound "keysight.ads.de.db.ParamItemCompound"). |
    | [`is_const`](#keysight.ads.de.db.ParamItem.is_const "keysight.ads.de.db.ParamItem.is_const")(p) | Return True if the ParamItem is a [`ParamItemConst`](keysight.ads.de.db.ParamItemConst.md#keysight.ads.de.db.ParamItemConst "keysight.ads.de.db.ParamItemConst"). |
    | [`is_null`](#keysight.ads.de.db.ParamItem.is_null "keysight.ads.de.db.ParamItem.is_null")(p) | Return True if the ParamItem is a [`ParamItemNull`](keysight.ads.de.db.ParamItemNull.md#keysight.ads.de.db.ParamItemNull "keysight.ads.de.db.ParamItemNull"). |
    | [`is_repeated`](#keysight.ads.de.db.ParamItem.is_repeated "keysight.ads.de.db.ParamItem.is_repeated")(p) | Return True if the ParamItem is a [`ParamItemRepeated`](keysight.ads.de.db.ParamItemRepeated.md#keysight.ads.de.db.ParamItemRepeated "keysight.ads.de.db.ParamItemRepeated"). |
    | [`is_string`](#keysight.ads.de.db.ParamItem.is_string "keysight.ads.de.db.ParamItem.is_string")(p) | Return True if the ParamItem is a [`ParamItemString`](keysight.ads.de.db.ParamItemString.md#keysight.ads.de.db.ParamItemString "keysight.ads.de.db.ParamItemString"). |

    Attributes

    |  |  |
    | --- | --- |
    | [`form_name`](#keysight.ads.de.db.ParamItem.form_name "keysight.ads.de.db.ParamItem.form_name") | The name of the [`Form`](keysight.ads.de.db.Form.md#keysight.ads.de.db.Form "keysight.ads.de.db.Form") that describes this item's value. |
    | [`name`](#keysight.ads.de.db.ParamItem.name "keysight.ads.de.db.ParamItem.name") | The name of the parameter. |
    | [`no_plot`](#keysight.ads.de.db.ParamItem.no_plot "keysight.ads.de.db.ParamItem.no_plot") | When True, this parameter will not be displayed in schematic view. |

    *property* name*: str*[](#keysight.ads.de.db.ParamItem.name "Link to this definition")
    :   The name of the parameter.

        For *normal* parameters, the name should match the name of a parameter
        definition in the model. If this is a default value, it doesn’t need a name.

    *property* form\_name*: str*[](#keysight.ads.de.db.ParamItem.form_name "Link to this definition")
    :   The name of the [`Form`](keysight.ads.de.db.Form.md#keysight.ads.de.db.Form "keysight.ads.de.db.Form") that describes this item’s value.

        The name must match one of the Forms in the parameter definition’s
        formset. Even when a ParamItem is not currently paired with its
        definition, many operations later associate the item with a
        [`ModelParam`](keysight.ads.de.db.ModelParam.md#keysight.ads.de.db.ModelParam "keysight.ads.de.db.ModelParam") (by parameter name); an invalid form name
        can cause errors at that point.

## 285. pypde\docs\reference\de\db\_autosummary\keysight.ads.de.db.ParamItemCompound.md {#pypde--docs--reference--de--db--_autosummary--keysight.ads.de.db.paramitemcompound}

# ParamItemCompound[](#paramitemcompound "Link to this heading")

*class* ParamItemCompound[](#keysight.ads.de.db.ParamItemCompound "Link to this definition")
:   Bases: [`ParamItem`](keysight.ads.de.db.ParamItem.md#keysight.ads.de.db.ParamItem "keysight.ads.de.db._parameters.ParamItem")

    A compound parameter item whose value consists of one or more sub-parameters.

    The number of sub-parameters must match the number of sub-parameters on the
    compound form that is used to create the parameter definition.
    The sub-parameters are typically related - for example, the name and value of a variable.

    Methods

    | --- | --- |

    |  |  |

    \_\_init\_\_(*param\_name: str*, *form\_name: str*, *subparams: Sequence[[ParamItem](keysight.ads.de.db.ParamItem.md#keysight.ads.de.db.ParamItem "keysight.ads.de.db._parameters.ParamItem")]*) → None[](#keysight.ads.de.db.ParamItemCompound.__init__ "Link to this definition")
    :   Initialize a ParamItemCompound.

        Parameters:
        :   * **param\_name** (*str*) – The name of the parameter.
            * **form\_name** (*str*) – The name of the form that describes this parameter’s value.
              This must be one of the forms in the parameter definition’s formset.
            * **subparams** (*Sequence[ParamItem]*) – The sub-parameters that make up this compound parameter’s value.

        Example

        ```
        def make_example_point_form() -> de.db.CompoundForm:
            formset = de.db.model_lib.formsets["StdFormSet"]
            param_default = de.db.std_string_param("0.0 mil")
            x_model_param = de.db.ModelParam("x", "x", formset)
            x_model_param.default_value = param_default
            y_model_param = de.db.ModelParam("y", "y", formset)
            y_model_param.default_value = param_default

            return de.db.CompoundForm("pointForm", "point", [x_model_param, y_model_param])

        point_form = make_example_point_form()
        param_x = de.db.std_string_param("10.0 mil")
        param_y = de.db.std_string_param("20.0 mil")
        sub_params = [param_x, param_y]
        point_param = de.db.ParamItemCompound("vertex", "pointForm", sub_params)
        ```

## 289. pypde\docs\reference\de\db\_autosummary\keysight.ads.de.db.ParamItemRepeated.md {#pypde--docs--reference--de--db--_autosummary--keysight.ads.de.db.paramitemrepeated}

# ParamItemRepeated[](#paramitemrepeated "Link to this heading")

*class* ParamItemRepeated[](#keysight.ads.de.db.ParamItemRepeated "Link to this definition")
:   Bases: [`ParamItem`](keysight.ads.de.db.ParamItem.md#keysight.ads.de.db.ParamItem "keysight.ads.de.db._parameters.ParamItem")

    A parameter item that holds a list of one or more repeats.

    The parameter definition’s formset dictates the forms that can be used for each repeat.
    A repeat cannot also be repeated but may use compound forms, having their own sub-parameters.
    The repeats of a repeatable parameter are typically independent of each other.

    :   Initialize a ParamItemRepeated.

        This is typically only needed when creating default values for
        a parameter definition of a repeated parameter.

        Parameters:

            * **repeats** (*Sequence[ParamItem]*) – The repeats that make up this repeated parameter’s value.
              There must be at least one repeat.

        Example

        ```
        # This example uses a string parameter.
        repeats = [de.db.std_string_param("0"), de.db.std_string_param("2")]        ]
        repeated_param = de.db.ParamItemRepeated("", repeats)
        ```

    An iterator that can be used to visit parameters of an instance or terminal.

    Methods

    |  |  |
    | --- | --- |
    | [`__init__`](#keysight.ads.de.db.ParamIter.__init__ "keysight.ads.de.db.ParamIter.__init__")() | Create a ParamIter for the given owner. |

    Attributes

    |  |  |
    | --- | --- |
    | [`definition`](#keysight.ads.de.db.ParamIter.definition "keysight.ads.de.db.ParamIter.definition") |  |

    | [`value`](#keysight.ads.de.db.ParamIter.value "keysight.ads.de.db.ParamIter.value") |  |

    \_\_init\_\_(*owner: InstanceDbu | InstanceUu*) → None[](#keysight.ads.de.db.ParamIter.__init__ "Link to this definition")

    \_\_init\_\_(*owner: TermBaseDbu | TermBaseUu*) → None
    :   Create a ParamIter for the given owner.

        Parameters:
        :   **owner** ([`Instance`](../../db_uu/_autosummary/keysight.ads.de.db_uu.Instance.md#keysight.ads.de.db_uu.Instance "keysight.ads.de.db_uu.Instance") | [`Term`](../../db_uu/_autosummary/keysight.ads.de.db_uu.Term.md#keysight.ads.de.db_uu.Term "keysight.ads.de.db_uu.Term")) – The instance or terminal whose parameters you want to iterate.

        Example

        ```
        # This assumes that inst is an :class:`~keysight.ads.de.db_uu.Instance`.
        for param in de.db.ParamIter(inst):
            print(f'Parameter "{param.item.name}" has value {param.value}')
        ```

    The repeats of a repeated parameter must be non-repeating.
    There must always be at least one repeat.

## 302. pypde\docs\reference\de\db\_autosummary\keysight.ads.de.db.CompoundForm.md {#pypde--docs--reference--de--db--_autosummary--keysight.ads.de.db.compoundform}

# CompoundForm[](#compoundform "Link to this heading")

*class* CompoundForm[](#keysight.ads.de.db.CompoundForm "Link to this definition")
:   Bases: [`Form`](keysight.ads.de.db.Form.md#keysight.ads.de.db.Form "keysight.ads.de.db._forms.Form")

    CompoundForm is a type of Form for a parameter that contains one or more sub-parameters.

    The CompoundForm describes how the parameter is netlisted and displayed.
    The Form for each sub-parameter describes how that portion of the parameter is netlisted and displayed.
    The number of sub-parameters is fixed by the parameter definition.

    | [`add_parameter`](#keysight.ads.de.db.CompoundForm.add_parameter "keysight.ads.de.db.CompoundForm.add_parameter")(parameter) | Add a sub-parameter to this CompoundForm. |

    \_\_init\_\_(*name: str*, *label: str = ''*, *params: Sequence[[ModelParam](keysight.ads.de.db.ModelParam.md#keysight.ads.de.db.ModelParam "keysight.ads.de.db._model_def.ModelParam")] = []*, *net\_format: str = ''*, *display\_format: str = ''*, *dialog\_data: str = ''*) → None[](#keysight.ads.de.db.CompoundForm.__init__ "Link to this definition")
    :   Initialize a CompoundForm.

        Parameters:
        :   * **name** (*str*) – Name of the form
            * **label** (*str*) – Descriptive label for the form.
            * **params** (*Sequence[ModelParam]*) – A sequence of sub-parameter definitions.
            * **net\_format** (*str*) – The netlist format string for values using this form.
              If empty, the default format string will be a comma separated list of sub-parameters.
            * **display\_format** (*str*) – The display format string for values using this form.
              If empty, the default format string will be a comma separated list of sub-parameters.
            * **dialog\_data** (*str*) – An optional string used by edit dialogs for this form.

        Example

        ```
        # A point is a compound form with two parameters, X and Y
        formset = de.db.model_lib.formsets["StdFormSet"]
        default_coordinate_value = de.db.std_string_param("0 mil")
        param_first = de.db.ModelParam("first", "x coordinate", formset)
        param_first.unit_type = de.db.ModelUnitType.LENGTH
        param_first.default_value = default_coordinate_value
        param_second = de.db.ModelParam("second", "y coordinate", formset)
        param_second.unit_type = de.db.ModelUnitType.LENGTH
        param_second.default_value = default_coordinate_value
        point_form = de.db.CompoundForm("PointForm", "x,y", [param_first, param_second])
        ```

    *property* parameters*: [NamedIndexedListRefAbc](../../_autosummary/keysight.ads.de._list_like.NamedIndexedListRefAbc.md#keysight.ads.de._list_like.NamedIndexedListRefAbc "keysight.ads.de._list_like.NamedIndexedListRefAbc")[[ModelParam](keysight.ads.de.db.ModelParam.md#keysight.ads.de.db.ModelParam "keysight.ads.de.db._model_def.ModelParam")]*[](#keysight.ads.de.db.CompoundForm.parameters "Link to this definition")

## 303. pypde\docs\reference\de\db\_autosummary\keysight.ads.de.db.Form.md {#pypde--docs--reference--de--db--_autosummary--keysight.ads.de.db.form}

# Form[](#form "Link to this heading")

*class* Form[](#keysight.ads.de.db.Form "Link to this definition")
:   Bases: `object`

    All parameter values are described by a Form that defines how the parameter is netlisted and displayed.

    A Form must appear in the Formset of a parameter definition in order
    to be usable by that parameter.
    See [`Formset`](keysight.ads.de.db.Formset.md#keysight.ads.de.db.Formset "keysight.ads.de.db.Formset") and class de.db.ModelParam.

    Common concrete Forms you typically create:
    - [`StringForm`](keysight.ads.de.db.StringForm.md#keysight.ads.de.db.StringForm "keysight.ads.de.db.StringForm")
    - [`ConstForm`](keysight.ads.de.db.ConstForm.md#keysight.ads.de.db.ConstForm "keysight.ads.de.db.ConstForm")
    - [`CompoundForm`](keysight.ads.de.db.CompoundForm.md#keysight.ads.de.db.CompoundForm "keysight.ads.de.db.CompoundForm")

# RepeatedForm[](#repeatedform "Link to this heading")

*class* RepeatedForm[](#keysight.ads.de.db.RepeatedForm "Link to this definition")
:   Bases: [`Form`](keysight.ads.de.db.Form.md#keysight.ads.de.db.Form "keysight.ads.de.db._forms.Form")

    RepeatedForm represents a parameter that is repeatable.

    There is only one RepeatedForm and its name is ‘list’.
    This form is used in the construction of a repeated parameter.
    The repeats of a repeatable parameter do not use this form, they
    use a form from the formset of that parameter’s definition.

    :   Validate and set the string value for the given parameter.

        Parameters:
        :   * **param** (*ParamItem*) – A parameter whose value is to be set.
              This parameter should have this form in its formset.
            * **value** (*str*) – The potential new value for the parameter.
            * **See :class:`StringFormWithCallbacks` and :class:`StringFormWithAELCallbacks`**
            * **for more information about validation callbacks.**
            * **If this form has a validation callback, it will be called to validate the value.**
            * **If the value is not valid, None will be returned.**
            * **If the parameter is not a string, a new ParamItemString will be returned**
            * **using this form and the given value.**
            * **Otherwise, the parameter will be returned after being updated**
            * **to use this form and the given value.**

    :   Initialize a StringFormWithCallbacks.

        Parameters:
        :   * **name** (*str*) – Name of the form
            * **label** (*str*) – Descriptive label for the form.
            * **net\_format** (*str*) – The netlist format string for values using this form.
              If empty, the default format string will be the name.
            * **display\_format** (*str*) – The display format string for values using this form.
              If empty, the default format string will be the name.
            * **dialog\_data** (*str*) – An optional string used by edit dialogs for this form.
            * **option\_cb** – An optional callback function that returns a list of valid
              options for a parameter.
            * **valid\_cb** – An optional callback function that validates a string value.
            * **data\_cb** – An optional callback function that returns a list of data
              strings for use in netlisting.

        Example

        ```
        def validate_width(value: str) -> bool:
            width = float(value.strip('"'))
            return 0.1 <= width <= 10.0

        def layer_lpp_names(design: de.db_uu.Design) -> list[str]:
            return ["cond:drawing", "cond2:drawing", "hold:drawing"]

        def layer_id_for_netlist(param: de.db.ParamItem, design: de.db_uu.Design) -> list[str]:
            assert isinstance(param, de.db.ParamItemString)
            # Example param.value: '"cond:drawing"'
            # Split the value into layer and purpose, stripping quotes
            layer, purpose = [s.strip('"') for s in param.value.split(":")]
            # Get the layer and return it
            layer_id = de.db.LayerId.from_name(design, layer, purpose)
            return [str(layer_id.layer)]

        # We don't need all three callbacks, this is just an example.
        form = de.db.StringFormWithCallbacks(
            "LayerTextForm",
            "LayerTextForm",
            "%d",
            "%v",
            "InstSelectionForm",
            layer_lpp_names,
            validate_width,
            layer_id_for_netlist,
        )
        ```

## 311. pypde\docs\reference\de\db\_autosummary\keysight.ads.de._pde.ModelParamType.md {#pypde--docs--reference--de--db--_autosummary--keysight.ads.de._pde.modelparamtype}

# ModelParamType[](#modelparamtype "Link to this heading")

*class* ModelParamType[](#keysight.ads.de._pde.ModelParamType "Link to this definition")
:   Bases: `Enum`

    Expected datatype for a parameter definition ([`ModelParam`](keysight.ads.de.db.ModelParam.md#keysight.ads.de.db.ModelParam "keysight.ads.de.db.ModelParam")).

    Parameter values are stored as strings, but client code sometimes
    expects a particular datatype when interpreting those strings (e.g.
    parsing a float vs an int, or treating the value as a complex number).

    This enum is metadata about the *intended* datatype; it does not, by itself,
    validate or convert values.

    Attributes

    |  |  |
    | --- | --- |
    | [`REAL`](#keysight.ads.de._pde.ModelParamType.REAL "keysight.ads.de._pde.ModelParamType.REAL") | Real-valued number (interpreted as a float). |
    | [`STRING`](#keysight.ads.de._pde.ModelParamType.STRING "keysight.ads.de._pde.ModelParamType.STRING") | String value (not intended to be parsed as a number). |
    | [`INT`](#keysight.ads.de._pde.ModelParamType.INT "keysight.ads.de._pde.ModelParamType.INT") | Integer-valued number. |
    | [`COMPLEX`](#keysight.ads.de._pde.ModelParamType.COMPLEX "keysight.ads.de._pde.ModelParamType.COMPLEX") | Complex-valued number (e.g., `2 + 3.5j`). |
    | [`REAL_ARRAY`](#keysight.ads.de._pde.ModelParamType.REAL_ARRAY "keysight.ads.de._pde.ModelParamType.REAL_ARRAY") | Array of real-valued numbers. |
    | [`INT_ARRAY`](#keysight.ads.de._pde.ModelParamType.INT_ARRAY "keysight.ads.de._pde.ModelParamType.INT_ARRAY") | Array of integer-valued numbers. |
    | [`STRING_ARRAY`](#keysight.ads.de._pde.ModelParamType.STRING_ARRAY "keysight.ads.de._pde.ModelParamType.STRING_ARRAY") | Array of strings. |
    | [`COMPLEX_ARRAY`](#keysight.ads.de._pde.ModelParamType.COMPLEX_ARRAY "keysight.ads.de._pde.ModelParamType.COMPLEX_ARRAY") | Array of complex-valued numbers. |
    | [`FIXED_POINT`](#keysight.ads.de._pde.ModelParamType.FIXED_POINT "keysight.ads.de._pde.ModelParamType.FIXED_POINT") | Fixed-point numeric value (e.g., `2.5`). |
    | [`FIXED_POINT_ARRAY`](#keysight.ads.de._pde.ModelParamType.FIXED_POINT_ARRAY "keysight.ads.de._pde.ModelParamType.FIXED_POINT_ARRAY") | Array of fixed-point numeric values (e.g., `2.4 3.6`). |
    | [`PRECISION_STRING`](#keysight.ads.de._pde.ModelParamType.PRECISION_STRING "keysight.ads.de._pde.ModelParamType.PRECISION_STRING") | Precision (e.g., `8.24` or `16/32`). |
    | [`UNSPECIFIED`](#keysight.ads.de._pde.ModelParamType.UNSPECIFIED "keysight.ads.de._pde.ModelParamType.UNSPECIFIED") | No specific datatype is declared; treat as tool-/client-defined. |

    REAL *= 'real'*[](#keysight.ads.de._pde.ModelParamType.REAL "Link to this definition")
    :   Real-valued number (interpreted as a float).

    STRING *= 'string'*[](#keysight.ads.de._pde.ModelParamType.STRING "Link to this definition")
    :   String value (not intended to be parsed as a number).

    INT *= 'int'*[](#keysight.ads.de._pde.ModelParamType.INT "Link to this definition")
    :   Integer-valued number.

    COMPLEX *= 'complex'*[](#keysight.ads.de._pde.ModelParamType.COMPLEX "Link to this definition")
    :   Complex-valued number (e.g., `2 + 3.5j`).

    REAL\_ARRAY *= 'realArray'*[](#keysight.ads.de._pde.ModelParamType.REAL_ARRAY "Link to this definition")
    :   Array of real-valued numbers.

    INT\_ARRAY *= 'intArray'*[](#keysight.ads.de._pde.ModelParamType.INT_ARRAY "Link to this definition")
    :   Array of integer-valued numbers.

    STRING\_ARRAY *= 'stringArray'*[](#keysight.ads.de._pde.ModelParamType.STRING_ARRAY "Link to this definition")
    :   Array of strings.

    COMPLEX\_ARRAY *= 'complexArray'*[](#keysight.ads.de._pde.ModelParamType.COMPLEX_ARRAY "Link to this definition")
    :   Array of complex-valued numbers.

    FIXED\_POINT *= 'fixed'*[](#keysight.ads.de._pde.ModelParamType.FIXED_POINT "Link to this definition")
    :   Fixed-point numeric value (e.g., `2.5`).

    FIXED\_POINT\_ARRAY *= 'fixedArray'*[](#keysight.ads.de._pde.ModelParamType.FIXED_POINT_ARRAY "Link to this definition")
    :   Array of fixed-point numeric values (e.g., `2.4 3.6`).

    PRECISION\_STRING *= 'precision'*[](#keysight.ads.de._pde.ModelParamType.PRECISION_STRING "Link to this definition")
    :   Precision (e.g., `8.24` or `16/32`).

    UNSPECIFIED *= 'unspecified'*[](#keysight.ads.de._pde.ModelParamType.UNSPECIFIED "Link to this definition")
    :   No specific datatype is declared; treat as tool-/client-defined.


---

## 312. pypde\docs\reference\de\db\_autosummary\keysight.ads.de._pde.ModelUnitType.md {#pypde--docs--reference--de--db--_autosummary--keysight.ads.de._pde.modelunittype}

# ModelUnitType[](#modelunittype "Link to this heading")

*class* ModelUnitType[](#keysight.ads.de._pde.ModelUnitType "Link to this definition")
:   Bases: `Enum`

    Unit types for parameter definitions (ModelParam).

    Each parameter defined by a ModelParam has a unit type. This describes
    the physical quantity (e.g., frequency or resistance) and drives how
    values are interpreted, displayed and scaled
    (e.g., Hz vs kHz vs MHz for [`FREQUENCY`](#keysight.ads.de._pde.ModelUnitType.FREQUENCY "keysight.ads.de._pde.ModelUnitType.FREQUENCY")).

    Attributes

    |  |  |
    | --- | --- |
    | [`STRING`](#keysight.ads.de._pde.ModelUnitType.STRING "keysight.ads.de._pde.ModelUnitType.STRING") | Value is a string. |
    | [`NO_UNIT`](#keysight.ads.de._pde.ModelUnitType.NO_UNIT "keysight.ads.de._pde.ModelUnitType.NO_UNIT") | Dimensionless numeric value (no units). |
    | [`FREQUENCY`](#keysight.ads.de._pde.ModelUnitType.FREQUENCY "keysight.ads.de._pde.ModelUnitType.FREQUENCY") | Frequency (e.g., Hz, MHz, GHz). |
    | [`RESISTANCE`](#keysight.ads.de._pde.ModelUnitType.RESISTANCE "keysight.ads.de._pde.ModelUnitType.RESISTANCE") | Resistance (e.g., Ohm, kOhm). |
    | [`CONDUCTANCE`](#keysight.ads.de._pde.ModelUnitType.CONDUCTANCE "keysight.ads.de._pde.ModelUnitType.CONDUCTANCE") | Conductance (e.g., S, uS). |
    | [`INDUCTANCE`](#keysight.ads.de._pde.ModelUnitType.INDUCTANCE "keysight.ads.de._pde.ModelUnitType.INDUCTANCE") | Inductance (e.g., H, nH). |
    | [`CAPACITANCE`](#keysight.ads.de._pde.ModelUnitType.CAPACITANCE "keysight.ads.de._pde.ModelUnitType.CAPACITANCE") | Capacitance (e.g., F, pF). |
    | [`LENGTH`](#keysight.ads.de._pde.ModelUnitType.LENGTH "keysight.ads.de._pde.ModelUnitType.LENGTH") | Length (e.g., meter, um, mil). |
    | [`TIME`](#keysight.ads.de._pde.ModelUnitType.TIME "keysight.ads.de._pde.ModelUnitType.TIME") | Time (e.g., sec, msec, nsec). |
    | [`ANGLE`](#keysight.ads.de._pde.ModelUnitType.ANGLE "keysight.ads.de._pde.ModelUnitType.ANGLE") | Angle (deg). |
    | [`POWER`](#keysight.ads.de._pde.ModelUnitType.POWER "keysight.ads.de._pde.ModelUnitType.POWER") | Power (e.g., W or dBm). |
    | [`VOLTAGE`](#keysight.ads.de._pde.ModelUnitType.VOLTAGE "keysight.ads.de._pde.ModelUnitType.VOLTAGE") | Voltage (e.g., V, mV). |
    | [`CURRENT`](#keysight.ads.de._pde.ModelUnitType.CURRENT "keysight.ads.de._pde.ModelUnitType.CURRENT") | Current (e.g., A, mA). |
    | [`DISTANCE`](#keysight.ads.de._pde.ModelUnitType.DISTANCE "keysight.ads.de._pde.ModelUnitType.DISTANCE") | Distance - typically long (e.g., km, miles). |
    | [`TEMPERATURE`](#keysight.ads.de._pde.ModelUnitType.TEMPERATURE "keysight.ads.de._pde.ModelUnitType.TEMPERATURE") | Temperature (Celsius). |
    | [`DB_GAIN`](#keysight.ads.de._pde.ModelUnitType.DB_GAIN "keysight.ads.de._pde.ModelUnitType.DB_GAIN") | Gain in decibels (dB). |
    | [`DATARATE`](#keysight.ads.de._pde.ModelUnitType.DATARATE "keysight.ads.de._pde.ModelUnitType.DATARATE") | Data rate (e.g., bps, Mbps, Gbps). |
    | [`PERCENT`](#keysight.ads.de._pde.ModelUnitType.PERCENT "keysight.ads.de._pde.ModelUnitType.PERCENT") | Percent (%). |

    STRING *= 'string'*[](#keysight.ads.de._pde.ModelUnitType.STRING "Link to this definition")
    :   Value is a string.

    NO\_UNIT *= 'num'*[](#keysight.ads.de._pde.ModelUnitType.NO_UNIT "Link to this definition")
    :   Dimensionless numeric value (no units).

    FREQUENCY *= 'freq'*[](#keysight.ads.de._pde.ModelUnitType.FREQUENCY "Link to this definition")
    :   Frequency (e.g., Hz, MHz, GHz).

    RESISTANCE *= 'res'*[](#keysight.ads.de._pde.ModelUnitType.RESISTANCE "Link to this definition")
    :   Resistance (e.g., Ohm, kOhm).

    CONDUCTANCE *= 'cond'*[](#keysight.ads.de._pde.ModelUnitType.CONDUCTANCE "Link to this definition")
    :   Conductance (e.g., S, uS).

    INDUCTANCE *= 'ind'*[](#keysight.ads.de._pde.ModelUnitType.INDUCTANCE "Link to this definition")
    :   Inductance (e.g., H, nH).

    CAPACITANCE *= 'cap'*[](#keysight.ads.de._pde.ModelUnitType.CAPACITANCE "Link to this definition")
    :   Capacitance (e.g., F, pF).

    LENGTH *= 'lng'*[](#keysight.ads.de._pde.ModelUnitType.LENGTH "Link to this definition")
    :   Length (e.g., meter, um, mil).

    TIME *= 'time'*[](#keysight.ads.de._pde.ModelUnitType.TIME "Link to this definition")
    :   Time (e.g., sec, msec, nsec).

    ANGLE *= 'ang'*[](#keysight.ads.de._pde.ModelUnitType.ANGLE "Link to this definition")
    :   Angle (deg).

    POWER *= 'power'*[](#keysight.ads.de._pde.ModelUnitType.POWER "Link to this definition")
    :   Power (e.g., W or dBm).

    VOLTAGE *= 'volt'*[](#keysight.ads.de._pde.ModelUnitType.VOLTAGE "Link to this definition")
    :   Voltage (e.g., V, mV).

    CURRENT *= 'cur'*[](#keysight.ads.de._pde.ModelUnitType.CURRENT "Link to this definition")
    :   Current (e.g., A, mA).

    DISTANCE *= 'dist'*[](#keysight.ads.de._pde.ModelUnitType.DISTANCE "Link to this definition")
    :   Distance - typically long (e.g., km, miles).

    TEMPERATURE *= 'temp'*[](#keysight.ads.de._pde.ModelUnitType.TEMPERATURE "Link to this definition")
    :   Temperature (Celsius).

    DB\_GAIN *= 'dbg'*[](#keysight.ads.de._pde.ModelUnitType.DB_GAIN "Link to this definition")
    :   Gain in decibels (dB).

    DATARATE *= 'datarate'*[](#keysight.ads.de._pde.ModelUnitType.DATARATE "Link to this definition")
    :   Data rate (e.g., bps, Mbps, Gbps).

    PERCENT *= 'pct'*[](#keysight.ads.de._pde.ModelUnitType.PERCENT "Link to this definition")
    :   Percent (%).

## 335. pypde\docs\reference\de\db\_autosummary\keysight.ads.de.db.Property.md {#pypde--docs--reference--de--db--_autosummary--keysight.ads.de.db.property}

# Property[](#property "Link to this heading")

*class* Property[](#keysight.ads.de.db.Property "Link to this definition")
:   Bases: `object`

    The base class for all properties.

    These properties live in a database, typically a design, but can also
    live in DM data files for Library, Cell, and View.

    To add a property to an object, you first choose the class for the Property,
    then initialize an object on the desired property owner.

    For example:
    de.db.StringProp.create(inst, “name”, “value”)

    To delete a property use delete\_prop.

## 348. pypde\docs\reference\de\db\_autosummary\keysight.ads.de.db_uu.Transaction.md {#pypde--docs--reference--de--db--_autosummary--keysight.ads.de.db_uu.transaction}

# Transaction[](#transaction "Link to this heading")

*class* Transaction[](#keysight.ads.de.db_uu.Transaction "Link to this definition")
:   Bases: `object`

    Operations performed between when the Transaction is created and when it is committed may be undone.

    This provides the ability to group multiple operations together and undo
    them with a call to rollback. Transactions are also important for schematics
    because the rule checker runs when the transaction is committed.

    Methods

    |  |  |
    | --- | --- |
    | [`__init__`](#keysight.ads.de.db_uu.Transaction.__init__ "keysight.ads.de.db_uu.Transaction.__init__")(design[, command]) |  |
    | [`commit`](#keysight.ads.de.db_uu.Transaction.commit "keysight.ads.de.db_uu.Transaction.commit")() | Commit the operations performed since the Transaction was created. |
    | [`is_empty`](#keysight.ads.de.db_uu.Transaction.is_empty "keysight.ads.de.db_uu.Transaction.is_empty")() |  |
    | [`rollback`](#keysight.ads.de.db_uu.Transaction.rollback "keysight.ads.de.db_uu.Transaction.rollback")() |  |

    Attributes

    |  |  |
    | --- | --- |
    | [`state`](#keysight.ads.de.db_uu.Transaction.state "keysight.ads.de.db_uu.Transaction.state") |  |

    \_\_init\_\_(*design: [Design](../../db_uu/_autosummary/keysight.ads.de.db_uu.Design.md#keysight.ads.de.db_uu.Design "keysight.ads.de.db_uu.Design") | DesignDb*, *command: str = 'Edit'*) → None[](#keysight.ads.de.db_uu.Transaction.__init__ "Link to this definition")

    commit() → None[](#keysight.ads.de.db_uu.Transaction.commit "Link to this definition")
    :   Commit the operations performed since the Transaction was created.

        This step is essential to make the operations permanent.

    rollback() → None[](#keysight.ads.de.db_uu.Transaction.rollback "Link to this definition")

    is\_empty() → bool[](#keysight.ads.de.db_uu.Transaction.is_empty "Link to this definition")

*class* Edge[](#keysight.ads.de.db.Edge "Link to this definition")
:   Bases: `object`

    A temporary object that represents the edge of an Outline.

    This edge should only be used as a temporary object. Any modifications

## 365. pypde\docs\reference\de\db\_autosummary\keysight.ads.de.db.Outline.md {#pypde--docs--reference--de--db--_autosummary--keysight.ads.de.db.outline}

# Outline[](#outline "Link to this heading")

*class* Outline[](#keysight.ads.de.db.Outline "Link to this definition")
:   Bases: `object`

    Represents a polyline composed of line and/or arc segments.

    It may represent either an open or closed shape.
    GenPolyline uses an Outline to represent an open shape.
    GenPolygon and GenPolygon\_with\_holes use an Outline to represent a closed shape.
    The points (vertices) and bulges control the shape of the outline.
    The edges are temporary objects that get invalidated whenever the Outline is modified.

# Transform[](#transform "Link to this heading")

*class* Transform[](#keysight.ads.de.db.Transform "Link to this definition")
:   Bases: `object`

    A helper class for transforming objects.

    The values of the offset (matrix.dx, matrix.dy), are unitless.
    If you use this Transform to transform a point or instance,
    the units of the offset must match the units of the point or instance.

## 368. pypde\docs\reference\de\db\_autosummary\keysight.ads.de._pde.BendStyle.md {#pypde--docs--reference--de--db--_autosummary--keysight.ads.de._pde.bendstyle}

# BendStyle[](#bendstyle "Link to this heading")

*class* BendStyle[](#keysight.ads.de._pde.BendStyle "Link to this definition")
:   Bases: `Enum`

    Defines the style of a bend in a polyline or polygon.

    Attributes

    |  |  |
    | --- | --- |
    | [`SQUARE`](#keysight.ads.de._pde.BendStyle.SQUARE "keysight.ads.de._pde.BendStyle.SQUARE") | `'Square'` The bend has square corners. |
    | [`CURVED`](#keysight.ads.de._pde.BendStyle.CURVED "keysight.ads.de._pde.BendStyle.CURVED") | `'Curved'` The bend has curved corners with a specified radius. |
    | [`MITERED`](#keysight.ads.de._pde.BendStyle.MITERED "keysight.ads.de._pde.BendStyle.MITERED") | `'Mitered'` The bend has mitered corners - prefer AdaptiveMitered. |
    | [`ADAPTIVE_MITERED`](#keysight.ads.de._pde.BendStyle.ADAPTIVE_MITERED "keysight.ads.de._pde.BendStyle.ADAPTIVE_MITERED") | `'AdaptiveMitered'` The bend has mitered corners with consistent cut length. |
    | [`NEW_MITERED`](#keysight.ads.de._pde.BendStyle.NEW_MITERED "keysight.ads.de._pde.BendStyle.NEW_MITERED") | `'AdaptiveMitered'` Deprecated alias for ADAPTIVE\_MITERED. |
    | [`ROUNDED`](#keysight.ads.de._pde.BendStyle.ROUNDED "keysight.ads.de._pde.BendStyle.ROUNDED") | `'Rounded'` The bend has rounded corners. |
    | [`EXACT_MITERED`](#keysight.ads.de._pde.BendStyle.EXACT_MITERED "keysight.ads.de._pde.BendStyle.EXACT_MITERED") | `'ExactMitered'` The bend has miter specified exactly - for internal use only. |
    | [`str`](#keysight.ads.de._pde.BendStyle.str "keysight.ads.de._pde.BendStyle.str") | Return the string representation of the bend style. |

    SQUARE *= 0*[](#keysight.ads.de._pde.BendStyle.SQUARE "Link to this definition")
    :   `'Square'` The bend has square corners.

    CURVED *= 1*[](#keysight.ads.de._pde.BendStyle.CURVED "Link to this definition")
    :   `'Curved'` The bend has curved corners with a specified radius.

    MITERED *= 2*[](#keysight.ads.de._pde.BendStyle.MITERED "Link to this definition")
    :   `'Mitered'` The bend has mitered corners - prefer AdaptiveMitered.

    ADAPTIVE\_MITERED *= 3*[](#keysight.ads.de._pde.BendStyle.ADAPTIVE_MITERED "Link to this definition")
    :   `'AdaptiveMitered'` The bend has mitered corners with consistent cut length.

    NEW\_MITERED *= 3*[](#keysight.ads.de._pde.BendStyle.NEW_MITERED "Link to this definition")
    :   `'AdaptiveMitered'` Deprecated alias for ADAPTIVE\_MITERED.

    ROUNDED *= 4*[](#keysight.ads.de._pde.BendStyle.ROUNDED "Link to this definition")
    :   `'Rounded'` The bend has rounded corners.

    EXACT\_MITERED *= 5*[](#keysight.ads.de._pde.BendStyle.EXACT_MITERED "Link to this definition")
    :   `'ExactMitered'` The bend has miter specified exactly - for internal use only.

    *property* str[](#keysight.ads.de._pde.BendStyle.str "Link to this definition")
    :   Return the string representation of the bend style.

## 396. pypde\docs\reference\de\db_uu\_autosummary\keysight.ads.de.db_uu.FigGroup.md {#pypde--docs--reference--de--db_uu--_autosummary--keysight.ads.de.db_uu.figgroup}

# FigGroup[](#figgroup "Link to this heading")

*class* FigGroup[](#keysight.ads.de.db_uu.FigGroup "Link to this definition")
:   Bases: [`Fig`](keysight.ads.de.db_uu.Fig.md#keysight.ads.de.db_uu.Fig "keysight.ads.de.db_uu._db_x.Fig")

    A collection of figures that can be reused.

    This collection is called a Group in the ADS UI.
    A Pin is considered to be a member of a FigGroup if all of its PinFigs are members.
    A composite object is considered to be a member of a FigGroup if all of its objects are members.

# PCBPad[](#pcbpad "Link to this heading")

*class* PCBPad[](#keysight.ads.de.db_uu.PCBPad "Link to this definition")
:   Bases: [`PCBBase`](keysight.ads.de.db_uu.PCBBase.md#keysight.ads.de.db_uu.PCBBase "keysight.ads.de.db_uu._db_x.PCBBase")

    Represents a PCB Pad instance in layout.

    The Pad can be a single layer pad, a pad with a specified drill layer,
    a pad with specified top and bottom layers, or a through pad.

## 410. pypde\docs\reference\de\db_uu\_autosummary\keysight.ads.de.db_uu.PCBVia.md {#pypde--docs--reference--de--db_uu--_autosummary--keysight.ads.de.db_uu.pcbvia}

# PCBVia[](#pcbvia "Link to this heading")

*class* PCBVia[](#keysight.ads.de.db_uu.PCBVia "Link to this definition")
:   Bases: [`PCBBase`](keysight.ads.de.db_uu.PCBBase.md#keysight.ads.de.db_uu.PCBBase "keysight.ads.de.db_uu._db_x.PCBBase")

    Represents a PCB Via instance in layout.

    The Via can be specified by rule or with a Padstack template definition
    and specified layers.
    Vias with Padstack definitions can have a specified drill layer,
    specified top and bottom layers, or be a through via.

    :   Name of the padstack template that defines this via.

    *property* rule\_name*: str*[](#keysight.ads.de.db_uu.PCBVia.rule_name "Link to this definition")
    :   Name of the via rule that defines this via.

# Via[](#via "Link to this heading")

*class* Via[](#keysight.ads.de.db_uu.Via "Link to this definition")
:   Bases: [`Ref`](keysight.ads.de.db_uu.Ref.md#keysight.ads.de.db_uu.Ref "keysight.ads.de.db_uu._db_x.Ref")

    Base class for OpenAccess Vias.

    A via represents a physical connection between traces (also PathSegs and Rountes)
    that are on two different layers. Vias are defined by a definition in the technology.

    flatten\_selected\_one\_level(*\**, *keep\_nets: bool = False*, *keep\_connectivity: bool = False*) → None[](#keysight.ads.de.db_uu.DesignEditor.flatten_selected_one_level "Link to this definition")
    :   Flatten the selected instances on the given design.

        keep\_nets:
        :   If True, nets from the top flattened designs are preserved.
            Also, shapes with InstTerms on the top level will pick up the nets from those InstTerms.

        keep\_connectivity:
        :   If True, the connectivity will be preserved.
            This means that shapes that were on the same net will still be on the same net and vice versa.

    flatten\_selected(*\**, *destination: [Design](keysight.ads.de.db_uu.Design.md#keysight.ads.de.db_uu.Design "keysight.ads.de.db_uu._design.Design") | None = None*, *include\_pins: bool = False*, *convert\_to\_polygons: bool = False*, *eliminate\_arcs: bool = False*, *keep\_nets: bool = False*, *keep\_connectivity: bool = False*) → None[](#keysight.ads.de.db_uu.DesignEditor.flatten_selected "Link to this definition")
    :   Flatten the instances on the design.

        mode:
        :   Specifies how much to flatten.
            By default, all levels of hierarchy are flattened.

        destination:
        :   If specified, the flattened objects are placed in this design.
            Otherwise, the objects are flattened in place.

        include\_pins:
        :   If True, pins from the top flattened designs are included.

        convert\_to\_polygons:
        :   If True, all shapes are converted to polygons or polylines when shapes are flattened.

        eliminate\_arcs:
        :   Only used when converting shapes to polygons or polylines.
            If True, arcs are converted to straight lines when shapes are converted.

        keep\_nets:
        :   If True, nets from the top flattened designs are preserved.
            Also, shapes with InstTerms on the top level will pick up the nets from those InstTerms.

        keep\_connectivity:
        :   If True, the connectivity will be preserved.
            This means that shapes that were on the same net will still be on the same net and vice versa.

    :   Explode the object at the given point.

    :   Break all selected objects.

    :   Swap the selected instances with the given item.

        item:

        keep\_params:

    :   Add all selected pin figs to the first pin of the specified term.

# LayerId[](#layerid "Link to this heading")

*class* LayerId[](#keysight.ads.de.db_uu.LayerId "Link to this definition")
:   Bases: `object`

    Represents the layer number and purpose number of objects in designs or technology.

    Figures on designs identify layers and purposes by their numbers.
    The numbers are used to find layers and purposes in the technology.
    The purpose is often “drawing”, so can often be omitted.

## 485. pypde\docs\reference\de\db_uu\_autosummary\keysight.ads.de.db_uu.create_layout.md {#pypde--docs--reference--de--db_uu--_autosummary--keysight.ads.de.db_uu.create_layout}

# create\_layout[](#create-layout "Link to this heading")

create\_layout(*name: CellviewRefLike*) → [Design](keysight.ads.de.db_uu.Design.md#keysight.ads.de.db_uu.Design "keysight.ads.de.db_uu._design.Design")[](#keysight.ads.de.db_uu.create_layout "Link to this definition")
:   Create a layout from an open library in the active workspace.

    Parameters:
    :   **name** (*CellviewRefLike*) – The name of the design, usually of the form “LibraryName:CellName:layout”

    Example

    ```
    >>> design = de.db_uu.create_layout(name=("test_lib", "test_2", "layout"))

        If no format string has been defined, will use an internally defined default
        format string, functionally equivalent to the below:

        ```
        builder.clear()
        builder.append_model_name()
        builder.append_str(":")
        builder.append_instance_name()
        builder.append_connectivity()
        builder.append_parameters()
        netlist_str = builder.netlist_str

        # OR:
        builder.clear()
        builder.append_model_and_instance_name()
        builder.append_connectivity()
        builder.append_parameters()
        netlist_str = builder.netlist_str
        ```

    append\_ordered\_item(*item\_name: str*) → None[](#keysight.ads.de.experimental._lpp.LppDb.append_ordered_item "Link to this definition")
    :   Append the referenced item ordered\_items.

        The item\_name must be a string in the form “layer:purpose”.
        If the referenced item already appears in the ordered\_items, it will be moved to the end.

    rearrange\_ordered\_items(*item\_names: Sequence[str]*) → None[](#keysight.ads.de.experimental._lpp.LppDb.rearrange_ordered_items "Link to this definition")
    :   Rearrange the ordered\_items to match the given order.

        The item\_names must be a list of strings in the form “layer:purpose”.
        If there are fewer item\_names than ordered\_items, the items referenced
        by item\_names will be moved to the front and the remaining items will be appended.

# DerivedLayer[](#derivedlayer "Link to this heading")

*class* DerivedLayer[](#keysight.ads.de.tech.DerivedLayer "Link to this definition")
:   Bases: [`Layer`](keysight.ads.de.tech.Layer.md#keysight.ads.de.tech.Layer "keysight.ads.de.tech._tech.Layer")

    Represents a derived layer.

    A derived layer is a (virtual) layer that is formed by operations on shapes
    from one or more other layers. Derived layers typically don’t have any shapes.

    | --- | --- |

    | [`create_sizing_layer`](#keysight.ads.de.tech.DerivedLayer.create_sizing_layer "keysight.ads.de.tech.DerivedLayer.create_sizing_layer")(tech, layer\_name, ...) | Create a derived layer from a single source layer, a sizing operation, and a distance parameter. |

## 561. pypde\docs\reference\de\tech\_autosummary\keysight.ads.de.tech.nested.LayerMap.md {#pypde--docs--reference--de--tech--_autosummary--keysight.ads.de.tech.nested.layermap}

# LayerMap[](#layermap "Link to this heading")

*class* LayerMap[](#keysight.ads.de.tech.nested.LayerMap "Link to this definition")
:   Bases: `object`

    LayerMap is a mapping of selected layers in a nested library to layers on the parent library.

    The nested library is assumed to have a different technology than the parent library.
    One or more layers from the nested library can be mapped to equivalent layers in the parent library.

    Methods

    |  |  |
    | --- | --- |
    | [`__init__`](#keysight.ads.de.tech.nested.LayerMap.__init__ "keysight.ads.de.tech.nested.LayerMap.__init__")(name, nested\_lib, parent\_lib) |  |
    | [`map_nested_layer`](#keysight.ads.de.tech.nested.LayerMap.map_nested_layer "keysight.ads.de.tech.nested.LayerMap.map_nested_layer")(nested\_layer\_name) | Add a mapping between the nested layer and a layer in the parent. |
    | [`unmap_nested_layer`](#keysight.ads.de.tech.nested.LayerMap.unmap_nested_layer "keysight.ads.de.tech.nested.LayerMap.unmap_nested_layer")(nested\_layer\_name) | Remove the mapping between for the nested layer. |

    Attributes

    |  |  |
    | --- | --- |
    | [`is_above`](#keysight.ads.de.tech.nested.LayerMap.is_above "keysight.ads.de.tech.nested.LayerMap.is_above") | Are the nested layers above the layers on the parent. |
    | [`is_flipped`](#keysight.ads.de.tech.nested.LayerMap.is_flipped "keysight.ads.de.tech.nested.LayerMap.is_flipped") | Are the nested layers flipped. |
    | [`layer_map_library_name`](#keysight.ads.de.tech.nested.LayerMap.layer_map_library_name "keysight.ads.de.tech.nested.LayerMap.layer_map_library_name") | The name of the layer mapped library. |
    | [`name`](#keysight.ads.de.tech.nested.LayerMap.name "keysight.ads.de.tech.nested.LayerMap.name") | The name of the layer mapping. |
    | [`nested_library_name`](#keysight.ads.de.tech.nested.LayerMap.nested_library_name "keysight.ads.de.tech.nested.LayerMap.nested_library_name") |  |
    | [`nested_mapped_layers`](#keysight.ads.de.tech.nested.LayerMap.nested_mapped_layers "keysight.ads.de.tech.nested.LayerMap.nested_mapped_layers") | Return the collection of nested mapped layer names in this LayerMap. |
    | [`parent_mapped_layers`](#keysight.ads.de.tech.nested.LayerMap.parent_mapped_layers "keysight.ads.de.tech.nested.LayerMap.parent_mapped_layers") | Return the collection of parent mapped layer names in this LayerMap. |

    \_\_init\_\_(*name: str*, *nested\_lib: str | [Library](../../_autosummary/keysight.ads.de.Library.md#keysight.ads.de.Library "keysight.ads.de.Library")*, *parent\_lib: str | [Library](../../_autosummary/keysight.ads.de.Library.md#keysight.ads.de.Library "keysight.ads.de.Library")*) → None[](#keysight.ads.de.tech.nested.LayerMap.__init__ "Link to this definition")

    *property* name*: str*[](#keysight.ads.de.tech.nested.LayerMap.name "Link to this definition")
    :   The name of the layer mapping. Used on nested substrate items.

    *property* nested\_library\_name*: str*[](#keysight.ads.de.tech.nested.LayerMap.nested_library_name "Link to this definition")

    *property* layer\_map\_library\_name*: str*[](#keysight.ads.de.tech.nested.LayerMap.layer_map_library_name "Link to this definition")
    :   The name of the layer mapped library. Usually the parent library name.

    *property* is\_above*: bool*[](#keysight.ads.de.tech.nested.LayerMap.is_above "Link to this definition")
    :   Are the nested layers above the layers on the parent.

    *property* is\_flipped*: bool*[](#keysight.ads.de.tech.nested.LayerMap.is_flipped "Link to this definition")
    :   Are the nested layers flipped.

    *property* nested\_mapped\_layers*: [ListRefAbc](../../_autosummary/keysight.ads.de._list_like.ListRefAbc.md#keysight.ads.de._list_like.ListRefAbc "keysight.ads.de._list_like.ListRefAbc")[str]*[](#keysight.ads.de.tech.nested.LayerMap.nested_mapped_layers "Link to this definition")
    :   Return the collection of nested mapped layer names in this LayerMap.

        These are the source layers from the nested library that are mapped.

    *property* parent\_mapped\_layers*: [ListRefAbc](../../_autosummary/keysight.ads.de._list_like.ListRefAbc.md#keysight.ads.de._list_like.ListRefAbc "keysight.ads.de._list_like.ListRefAbc")[str]*[](#keysight.ads.de.tech.nested.LayerMap.parent_mapped_layers "Link to this definition")
    :   Return the collection of parent mapped layer names in this LayerMap.

        These are the mapped layers in the parent library.

    map\_nested\_layer(*nested\_layer\_name: str*) → None[](#keysight.ads.de.tech.nested.LayerMap.map_nested_layer "Link to this definition")
